subject: measurement invariance in longitudinal CFA with categorical data

messages.author: 7d1ac766483df74a
messages.subject: measurement invariance in longitudinal CFA with categorical data
parts:
Hello, 
Does anyone know if assessing weak (loadings) and strong (thresholds) invariance can be done properly in lavaan?

I have something like this. I compare m1 and m2 (in this case, I omit residual correlations):

m1 <- ' 
f1_1 ~= var1_1 + var2_1 + var3_1
f2_1 ~= var4_1 + var5_1 + var6_1

f1_2 ~= var1_2 + var2_2 + var3_2
f2_2 ~= var4_2 + var5_2 + var6_2'

m2 <- ' 
f1_1 ~= f1*var1_1 + f2*var2_1 + f3*var3_1
f2_1 ~= f4* var4_1 + f5*var5_1 + f6*var6_1

f1_2 ~= f1*var1_2 + f2*var2_2 + f3*var3_2
f2_2 ~= f4*var4_2 + f5*var5_2 + f6*var6_2'

I cannot reject this test (p=0.943), so loadings would be invariant. Is that conclusion right?

When I use theta parameterization in Mplus (therefore, a different model) I get different conclusions: I cannot support weak invariance. 
My Mplus test (allowing free factors means, residual variances, and some restrictions in thresholds for identification) is better or more accurate regarding weak invariance?

Any thoughts, suggestions or references would be very appreciated. 
Thanks

messages.author: 363dfa4f3e23fb33
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance in longitudinal CFA with categorical data
parts:
i think you can add the following to make thresholds invariant between var1_1 and var1_2 (assuming 3 categories):

var1_1 | th1*t1 + th2*t2
var1_2 | th1*t1 + th2*t2

messages.author: 7df2156b01b2e0da
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance in longitudinal CFA with categorical data
parts:
Dear lavaan-ers,

I am trying to explore the latent mean change of my model. I'll add below an example model and will attach simulated data (be aware the data fits really bad, but it should be ok for illustrative purposes I hope).

I equated the item loadings and thresholds for items across the two modeled time points. I fixed the first latent variance to 1 and estimated the loading of the first items (NB: as the first items have been defined as having an equal loading across the two time points, I think only one loading parameter needs to be estimated, which is why I fixed only one latent factor variance two 1 and not both).

Model1 <- 'Factor_t1 =~ NA*x1t1 + aa*x1t1 + bb*x2t1 + cc*x3t1
                 Factor_t2 =~ NA*x1t2 + aa*x1t2 + bb*x2t2 + cc*x3t2
 Factor_t1 ~~ 1*Factor_t1
 x1t1 ~~ x1t2
 x2t1 ~~ x2t2
 x3t1 ~~ x3t2
 x1t1 | c(a)*t1 + c(b)*t2 + c(c)*t3
 x1t2 | c(a)*t1 + c(b)*t2 + c(c)*t3
 x2t1 | c(d)*t1 + c(e)*t2 + c(f)*t3
 x2t2 | c(d)*t1 + c(e)*t2 + c(f)*t3
 x3t1 | c(i)*t1 + c(j)*t2 + c(k)*t3
 x3t2 | c(i)*t1 + c(j)*t2 + c(k)*t3'
fit1 <- cfa(Model1, data = mydata,  estimator="WLSMV", ordered=c("x1t1", "x2t1", "x3t1","x1t2", "x2t2", "x3t2"))
results1 <- summary(fit1, fit.measures=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

To investigate the difference in the two latent means, I set the mean of the first factor to "0" and let the second latent factor mean be freely estimated:

 Model2 <- 'Factor_t1 =~ NA*x1t1 + aa*x1t1 + bb*x2t1 + cc*x3t1
                   Factor_t2 =~ NA*x1t2 + aa*x1t2 + bb*x2t2 + cc*x3t2
 Factor_t1 ~~ 1*Factor_t1
 Factor_t1 ~ 0*1
 Factor_t2 ~ NA*1
 x1t1 ~~ x1t2
 x2t1 ~~ x2t2
 x3t1 ~~ x3t2
 x1t1 | c(a)*t1 + c(b)*t2 + c(c)*t3
 x1t2 | c(a)*t1 + c(b)*t2 + c(c)*t3
 x2t1 | c(d)*t1 + c(e)*t2 + c(f)*t3
 x2t2 | c(d)*t1 + c(e)*t2 + c(f)*t3
 x3t1 | c(i)*t1 + c(j)*t2 + c(k)*t3
 x3t2 | c(i)*t1 + c(j)*t2 + c(k)*t3'
 fit2 <- cfa(Model2, data = mydata,  estimator="WLSMV", ordered=c("x1t1", "x2t1", "x3t1","x1t2", "x2t2", "x3t2"))
 results2 <- summary(fit2, fit.measures=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)
 
The results show that I have a standardized mean difference of -0.304.

Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
    Factor_t1         0.000                               0.000    0.000
    Factor_t2        -0.181    0.033   -5.456    0.000   -0.304   -0.304

Next I fixed both instead of one latent factor variances to 1, as in the following model:

Model3 <- 'Factor_t1 =~ NA*x1t1 + aa*x1t1 + bb*x2t1 + cc*x3t1
                 Factor_t2 =~ NA*x1t2 + aa*x1t2 + bb*x2t2 + cc*x3t2
 Factor_t1 ~~ 1*Factor_t1
 Factor_t2 ~~ 1*Factor_t2
 Factor_t1 ~ 0*1
 Factor_t2 ~ NA*1
 x1t1 ~~ x1t2
 x2t1 ~~ x2t2
 x3t1 ~~ x3t2
 x1t1 | c(a)*t1 + c(b)*t2 + c(c)*t3
 x1t2 | c(a)*t1 + c(b)*t2 + c(c)*t3
 x2t1 | c(d)*t1 + c(e)*t2 + c(f)*t3
 x2t2 | c(d)*t1 + c(e)*t2 + c(f)*t3
 x3t1 | c(i)*t1 + c(j)*t2 + c(k)*t3
 x3t2 | c(i)*t1 + c(j)*t2 + c(k)*t3'
fit3 <- cfa(Model3, data = mydata,  estimator="WLSMV", ordered=c("x1t1", "x2t1", "x3t1","x1t2", "x2t2", "x3t2"))
results3 <- summary(fit3, fit.measures=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

Then I get a standardized latent mean difference of -0.214.

Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
    Factor_t1         0.000                               0.000    0.000
    Factor_t2        -0.214    0.039   -5.452    0.000   -0.214   -0.214

I am now a little bit stuck with interpreting the difference between the change in latent mean prior to vs after fixing the second latent factor variance to 1.

Can anyone perhaps shed light on the different interpretations of the latent mean change in the two models?

Thank you very much!

Jes

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance in longitudinal CFA with categorical data
parts: Can anyone perhaps shed light on the different interpretations of the latent mean change in the two models?

You have categorical items, so the mean and covariance structures are no longer independent, as they would be with multinormal data.

You did not release the constraints on the variances of the latent item responses when you constrained thresholds to equality, so you are implicitly assuming invariance of their total variances (check the Scales in the summary() output to see they are all 1).  The residual variances will differ in the output, but they are not free parameters when using the default parameterization = "delta", so they are still constrained as a function of the total variances and the factor loadings. 

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

In multiple-group models, the variances in the second group would have been freed when using the argument group.equal = "thresholds", but obviously that is not an option when constraining across occasions of measurement within the same group, so you need to free them manually.  When you add the constraint that the second factor's variance == 1, that misspecification will affect other model parameters, perhaps causing the counterintuitive result you see.

If you are unfamiliar with the complex identification issues involved with categorical CFA, consider using my new semTools function to print syntax so you can see what should happen when you constrain thresholds (also see the References in the ?measEq.syntax help page).

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/oKwP0_6-i1g/i0jGCU-LBwAJ

Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
